title: Deposit Window Levels and the Checking Component of a Personal Checking Relationship Balance
content:
Two cases change what the checking component of a Personal Checking relationship balance is taken from, read from a premier money market balance held under Savings & Money Market Accounts, from the owner's card payments under Personal Credit Cards and from certificate principal held under Certificates of Deposit.

- Where the owner's premier money market balance reaches the protection source minimum of 5000.00 **and** the owner has made at least 6 card payments in the last twelve months, the total of the credits the account has taken in over the deposit window is taken. The deposit window runs back 3 calendar months from the day the matter is handled.
- Where the case above does not apply **and** either the owner's certificate principal is above zero **or** the owner has made at least 3 card payments in the last twelve months, half of the credits the account has taken in over the deposit window is taken.
- Where neither case applies, the checking component is not taken from the deposit window in either of those ways.

**Worked treatments on hypothetical inputs.** An account has taken in credits of 6200.00 over the deposit window.

| Owner's position | Checking component |
|---|---|
| Premier money market balance of 9000.00, 8 card payments in the last twelve months | 6200.00 |
| Premier money market balance of 900.00, 8 card payments | 3100.00 |
| Premier money market balance of 900.00, 1 card payment, certificate principal of 2000.00 | 3100.00 |
| Premier money market balance of 900.00, 1 card payment, no certificate principal | Neither case applies |

A credit posted one day before the deposit window opens falls outside it and enters neither case's figure. Equality satisfies each threshold, so a premier money market balance of exactly 5000.00 with exactly 6 card payments reaches the first case.
